result.title: FaceNet versus VGG Features in Wasserstein Distortion for Face Image Compression
result.summary: Wasserstein distortion (WD) compares local statistics of deep features and has been used to optimize learned image codecs for perceptual quality, but existing WD objectives rely on features from networks trained for generic image classification, such as VGG. We ask whether features from a face recognition network better reflect the perceived quality of compressed faces. In the Cool-Chic codec, we replace the VGG features in a WD-based objective with intermediate feature maps of FaceNet, and compare the two objectives on 20 LFW face images at a matched average bitrate of about 0.15 bits per pixel. In a preliminary pairwise human study, FaceNet-based reconstructions were preferred in 72.5% of judgments and by a majority of participants on 16 of the 20 images. These results suggest that the choice of feature network inside WD affects the perceived quality of face images, and that face recognition features are a promising direction for face-aware perceptual compression.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在 Cool-Chic 编解码器中把 Wasserstein 失真目标里的 VGG 特征替换为 FaceNet 中间特征，在约 0.15 bpp 的匹配码率下比较 20 张 LFW 人脸图像，并用初步成对人工评测显示 FaceNet 版本在 72.5% 的判断中被偏好。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作不涉及视觉推理或 latent 状态生成，但它说明换用不同网络、不同中间层特征会改变基于特征距离的评价结论，这一线索可能供核查 LVR 中 latent 相似度对特征来源与深度的敏感性。
